description:
INTEGER_COMPARAND_RE covers -eq/-ge/-le/== but omits -gt, -lt, -ne and !=. `test $X -gt 41` is the identical frozen-comparand defect and slips through unflagged. This matches the PRD notes verbatim ('-eq/-ge/-le/== N'), so it is spec-conformant rather than a deviation, but it leaves a real coverage gap in the rule's stated purpose. Worth a follow-up issue widening the operator alternation plus a flagged-forms test per added operator.

Source: cam/issue-381
Review round: 1

suggestion-fingerprint: a8557d3c9660

spec.scope:
UMBRELLA over CAM-382, CAM-383, CAM-384 and CAM-385. All four land in src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts and its single test file test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts; they are separate issues only because `cam suggestions promote` is single-fingerprint, which is a filing-time constraint, not an implementation-time one. CAM-382 and CAM-383 rewrite the same function (hasFrozenIntegerComparand, L164-171) and CAM-384/CAM-385 touch lines those edits pass through, so shipping them sequentially would have each cycle churn the previous one's code. Close all four at ship.

This is the honest completion of CAM-381 (PR #302), which shipped the frozen-comparand rule but left it missing its own motivating example.

FOUR PARTS.

(1) CAM-382 -- widen the operator alternation. INTEGER_COMPARAND_RE at src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts:154 is /(?:-eq|-ge|-le|==)\s*\d+\b/. It omits -ne, -gt, -lt and !=. `test $X -gt 41` is the identical frozen-comparand defect and is exactly the shape of CAM-377, the defect that motivated the whole derive-don't-freeze rule, so the rule as shipped does not catch the case it was written for. Add all four operators. While editing that exact regex, also add a LEFT boundary: the alternation currently has \b only after \d+, so a mid-token operator such as the `-eq` inside `foo-eq 42` or a `--ge 5` long-flag matches and produces a false positive. Widening the alternation without the left anchor compounds that on the very line being edited, so it is in scope here and only here.

(2) CAM-383 -- scope the derivation excuse per clause instead of per whole command. hasFrozenIntegerComparand (L168-171) is two whole-string boolean tests: `if (!INTEGER_COMPARAND_RE.test(command)) return false; return !LIVE_DERIVATION_RE.test(command);`. There is no positional comparison, no enumeration of matches and no splitting, so ANY live-derivation token anywhere in the command excuses EVERY integer comparand in it, and at most one finding is ever emitted per command. A mixed oracle such as `test $(git show main:a.ts | wc -l) -ge 1 && test $(wc -l < b.ts) -eq 42` hides the genuinely frozen 42 behind the unrelated live token in the first clause.

DIRECTION, resolved on measurement, do not re-litigate: split the command into clauses on `&&`, `||`, `;` and newline, and excuse an integer comparand only when a live-derivation token appears in the SAME clause. The stronger reading -- that an operator followed by a literal integer is frozen unconditionally, with no escape hatch at all -- was considered and REJECTED because it over-flags: it would flag `-ge 1` style sanity floors, which never rot, and it would redden the existing legitimate passing test at test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts:213-218 whose first clause is `test $(git show main:file.ts | wc -l) -ge 1`. Clause-level scoping catches the filed motivating example while leaving that test green.

(3) CAM-384 -- rename the misleading test at test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts:200-203. It is named 'does not match main by literal substring -- mainbranch is not the main token' but sits in the 'flagged forms' describe and asserts `.not.toBeNull()`. The assertion is correct; the 'does not' phrasing reads as a negative case and inverts the reader's expectation against the surrounding convention, where 'flags X' marks positive cases and 'does not flag X' marks negative ones. Rename to the positive form, e.g. 'flags a mainbranch: ref, which is not the main token'.

(4) CAM-385 -- reword the doc comment on hasUnguardedSedLineAnchor. It states the guard must 'precede' the sed anchor ('no test -n "$VAR" / [ -n "$VAR" ] guard for that exact variable name precedes it anywhere in the command'), but the function applies guardRe to the whole command string with no positional constraint, so a guard appearing AFTER the anchor also suppresses the finding. The permissive runtime behavior is the defensible one and must NOT change; only the comment is wrong. Reword the comment to match measured behavior, per the standing project lesson that a comment does not prove runtime behavior.

OUT OF SCOPE, already filed separately, do NOT touch: CAM-386 (LIVE_DERIVATION_RE's \bmain\b matches the 'main' inside the filename 'main.ts', so `git grep PATTERN main.ts` falsely counts as a derivation token). That is about WHAT QUALIFIES as a derivation token; CAM-383 is about WHICH comparands a token excuses. Per-clause scoping does not fix it and must not attempt to.
acceptanceCriteria: INTEGER_COMPARAND_RE in src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts matches all eight comparison operators -eq, -ne, -gt, -lt, -ge, -le, == and !=, each when followed by optional whitespace and a literal integer. Falsifiable behaviorally, not by grep: for EACH of the four newly added operators, the frozen-comparand rule returns a non-null finding for a single-clause command of that shape with no derivation token present. All four of these are red against unmodified main.

INTEGER_COMPARAND_RE does not match an operator embedded mid-token: the frozen-comparand rule returns null for a command whose only operator-like text is a longer token containing it (for example a `--ge 5` long flag, and an identifier ending in the operator such as `foo-eq 42`). Red against unmodified main, which lacks any left boundary and therefore flags both.

The derivation excuse is scoped per clause. The frozen-comparand rule returns a NON-NULL finding for the mixed oracle `test $(git show main:a.ts | wc -l) -ge 1 && test $(wc -l < b.ts) -eq 42`, in which the second clause carries a frozen 42 and no derivation token of its own. Red against unmodified main, where the whole-command LIVE_DERIVATION_RE check excuses it and yields null.

PINNING CRITERION, deliberately GREEN against main and labelled as such rather than laundered as red: the pre-existing passing case at test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts:213-218 still returns null. Its first clause pairs a `git show main:` derivation with a `-ge 1` sanity floor in the SAME clause, so clause-level scoping must leave it excused. This criterion exists to prove the widening did not over-flag; if it goes red, the implementation chose the rejected no-escape-hatch direction.

Every one of the four rules in RULES is still present and named exactly as on main: grep-q-plus-list-files, frozen-comparand, rotating-artifact-target, zero-match-vacuous. RULES.length is unchanged from main's value, derived live from main at check time rather than compared against a frozen literal. This slice strengthens one existing rule; it adds no rule and removes none.

The frozen-comparand flagged-forms and passing-cases describe blocks gain at least one test per newly covered operator and at least one test for the mixed-clause case. The total test count in test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts strictly EXCEEDS main's count, with main's count derived live at check time via git show rather than frozen as a literal. No existing test is deleted or weakened; if the assertion count on main is X, the assertion count after must be greater than X.

The test at test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts:200-203 no longer carries a name beginning 'does not match', and its assertion remains `.not.toBeNull()` with its command string byte-unchanged. The rename must change only the test name, not the case it exercises.

The doc comment on hasUnguardedSedLineAnchor no longer claims the guard must 'precede' the anchor, and the function body's guard-matching logic is byte-unchanged from main. Verify the body is unchanged by extracting the function from both main and the branch and diffing them: the comment moves, the behavior does not.

MODULE PURITY PRESERVED, the hard contract this module declares at its header: src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts still has exactly two import statements and introduces no fs, node:fs, Bun.file, Bun.spawn, Bun.$, Bun.write or child_process usage. The exported surface is unchanged: RuleFinding, OracleLintRule, PrdOracleLintFinding, RULES and lintPrd remain exported, lintStoryCriteria remains module-private, and lintPrd's signature is byte-identical to main's.

Quality gates green: bun run typecheck zero errors, bun test with zero failures, bun run check:all passing. The total passing test count strictly exceeds main's 5229 baseline, derived live rather than compared against a frozen literal, and the failure count is zero.
gotchas: prd-oracle-lint.ts is SIDECAR-EXECUTED at plan time: lintPrd is called from src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:804 via runOracleLintCheck, invoked at plan-runner.ts:1036 between the planner's prd.json presence guard (L1029) and the auditor spawn (L1042). A rebuild plus sidecar respawn is therefore MANDATORY after merge, or the operator's own plan preflights keep running the old under-enforcing rule.

This module lints acceptance criteria. The criteria written FOR this story are themselves subject to the four rules it implements, including the very frozen-comparand rule being widened here. Do not author a criterion comparing against a frozen literal count; derive every main-derived comparand at check time.

Prefer BEHAVIORAL oracles over grep oracles throughout this story: import RULES, find the rule by name, and call rule.test(command) directly. A grep for a regex source string is fragile and has repeatedly produced non-falsifiable oracles in this repo. Behavioral checks against the real exported rule are both stronger and simpler here.

Every acceptance oracle must be swept RED against unmodified main before it is trusted, exhaustively rather than by sample; the one deliberately-green pinning criterion is labelled as such in its own text and must not be reported as red.

Neither src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts (394 lines) nor test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts (508 lines) appears in scripts/file-size-budget.json, so there is no ceiling to raise for either. Do not add budget entries.

The test file's naming convention is 'flags X' for positive cases and 'does not flag X' for negative ones, with describe blocks named '<rule-name> rule: flagged forms' and '<rule-name> rule: passing cases', and the rule handle bound once per describe via findFrozenComparandRule(). Follow it for every added test; CAM-384 exists precisely because one test violated it.

LIVE_DERIVATION_RE itself is OUT OF SCOPE and must be left byte-unchanged. Its \bmain\b looseness is filed as CAM-386. Clause-level scoping changes only WHERE the existing regex is applied, never what it matches.

hasFrozenIntegerComparand currently emits at most one finding per command. Clause-level scoping makes multiple frozen comparands possible in one command; decide deliberately whether the rule still returns a single RuleFinding (the OracleLintRule contract returns RuleFinding | null, so it must) and make the reason text accurate when more than one clause is at fault.
domainTerms: frozen comparand: an acceptance-criterion oracle comparing against a literal integer captured once at authoring time, which rots silently when a later commit on main edits the compared file.
live derivation token: a `git show main:<path>`, `git diff main` or `git grep ... main` invocation that recomputes a comparand against main at check time instead of freezing it.
clause: a segment of a shell oracle command delimited by &&, ||, ; or newline; the unit at which the derivation excuse is scoped after this slice.

pinning criterion: an acceptance criterion deliberately green against main, present to prove an existing behavior did NOT change, as opposed to the normal red-against-main criterion proving new behavior was added.
